```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)

# Paths relative to this Rmd's location (Adriana_analysis/scripts/)
project_dir <- ".."
load(file.path(project_dir, "project_functions.rda"))

paths       <- setup_project_paths(project_dir)
tables_dir  <- paths$tables_dir
figures_dir <- paths$figures_dir
output_dir  <- paths$output_dir
```

```{r libraries}
library(tidyverse)
library(clusterProfiler)
library(org.Sc.sgd.db)   # S. cerevisiae annotation

# org.Sc.sgd.db loads AnnotationDbi, which masks dplyr::select() -
# pin select() back to the dplyr version explicitly to avoid
# "unable to find an inherited method" errors on tibbles
select <- dplyr::select

# Shared colour palette for dissertation figures
load(file.path(project_dir, "project_colours.rda"))
```

```{r load-data}
# PCA_genes_AC.txt holds gene-level PC scores (gene_id, PC1...PC93).
# PC1-PC3 are confirmed the only biologically meaningful axes; PC1/PC2
# match the stress-response pattern Adriana described (analogous to the
# WT vs Torin/PhIAA-perturbed size-dependent trend). PC4 onward is noise.
pca_genes <- read_tsv(file.path(tables_dir, "PCA_genes_AC.txt"), show_col_types = FALSE)

pca_genes_long <- pca_genes %>%
  select(gene_id, PC1, PC2) %>%
  pivot_longer(c(PC1, PC2), names_to = "PC", values_to = "score")
```

```{r filter-top-bottom-10pct}
# Take top/bottom 10% of PC1 and PC2 separately, per Adriana's original
# approach (known limitation: a hard 10% cutoff can split genes with
# near-identical scores - GSEA in script 03 addresses this instead)
get_top_bottom_10pct <- function(df, pc_name) {
  df_pc <- df %>% filter(PC == pc_name)
  n <- nrow(df_pc)
  cutoff_n <- ceiling(n * 0.1)

  top <- df_pc %>% slice_max(score, n = cutoff_n) %>% pull(gene_id)
  bottom <- df_pc %>% slice_min(score, n = cutoff_n) %>% pull(gene_id)

  list(top = top, bottom = bottom)
}

pc1_genes <- get_top_bottom_10pct(pca_genes_long, "PC1")
pc2_genes <- get_top_bottom_10pct(pca_genes_long, "PC2")

cat("PC1 top 10%:", length(pc1_genes$top), "genes | bottom 10%:", length(pc1_genes$bottom), "genes\n")
cat("PC2 top 10%:", length(pc2_genes$top), "genes | bottom 10%:", length(pc2_genes$bottom), "genes\n")
```

```{r run-enrichment-function}
# Wrapper for enrichGO, reused across PC1/PC2 and top/bottom
run_go_enrichment <- function(gene_list, universe, label) {
  ego <- enrichGO(
    gene          = gene_list,
    universe      = universe,
    OrgDb         = org.Sc.sgd.db,
    keyType       = "ORF",
    ont           = "ALL",
    pAdjustMethod = "BH",
    pvalueCutoff  = 0.05,
    qvalueCutoff  = 0.2
  )
  cat(label, "-", nrow(as.data.frame(ego)), "enriched terms\n")
  ego
}

all_genes_universe <- pca_genes$gene_id
```

```{r run-pc1}
ego_pc1_top    <- run_go_enrichment(pc1_genes$top,    all_genes_universe, "PC1 top 10%")
ego_pc1_bottom <- run_go_enrichment(pc1_genes$bottom, all_genes_universe, "PC1 bottom 10%")
```

```{r run-pc2}
ego_pc2_top    <- run_go_enrichment(pc2_genes$top,    all_genes_universe, "PC2 top 10%")
ego_pc2_bottom <- run_go_enrichment(pc2_genes$bottom, all_genes_universe, "PC2 bottom 10%")
```

```{r plot-function}
# Plot top 20 terms by p-value, per Adriana's original plotting approach.
# Long GO term names (e.g. some rRNA processing terms) can push the whole
# plot off-canvas - truncate + wrap to avoid this
plot_top20_terms <- function(ego, title) {
  df <- as.data.frame(ego)
  if (nrow(df) == 0) {
    cat("No enriched terms for:", title, "\n")
    return(NULL)
  }

  df_top20 <- df %>%
    arrange(p.adjust) %>%
    slice_head(n = 20) %>%
    mutate(
      Description_short = truncate_wrap_description(Description),
      Description_short = fct_reorder(Description_short, -log10(p.adjust)),
      neg_log10_padj = -log10(p.adjust)
    )

  ggplot(df_top20, aes(x = neg_log10_padj, y = Description_short, size = Count)) +
    geom_point(color = project_colours["blue"]) +
    labs(
      title = title,
      x = expression(-log[10]("adjusted p-value")),
      y = NULL
    ) +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(axis.text.y = element_text(size = 8))
}
```

```{r plot-pc1, fig.width=9, fig.height=8}
plot_top20_terms(ego_pc1_top,    "PC1 top 10% - GO enrichment (clusterProfiler)")
plot_top20_terms(ego_pc1_bottom, "PC1 bottom 10% - GO enrichment (clusterProfiler)")
```

```{r plot-pc2, fig.width=9, fig.height=8}
plot_top20_terms(ego_pc2_top,    "PC2 top 10% - GO enrichment (clusterProfiler)")
plot_top20_terms(ego_pc2_bottom, "PC2 bottom 10% - GO enrichment (clusterProfiler)")
```

```{r save-outputs}
# Save results tables and figures
write_tsv(as.data.frame(ego_pc1_top),    file.path(output_dir, "go_clusterprofiler_pc1_top10pct.txt"))
write_tsv(as.data.frame(ego_pc1_bottom), file.path(output_dir, "go_clusterprofiler_pc1_bottom10pct.txt"))
write_tsv(as.data.frame(ego_pc2_top),    file.path(output_dir, "go_clusterprofiler_pc2_top10pct.txt"))
write_tsv(as.data.frame(ego_pc2_bottom), file.path(output_dir, "go_clusterprofiler_pc2_bottom10pct.txt"))

for (pc_label in c("pc1_top", "pc1_bottom", "pc2_top", "pc2_bottom")) {
  ego_obj <- get(paste0("ego_", pc_label))
  p <- plot_top20_terms(ego_obj, paste(toupper(pc_label), "- GO enrichment"))
  if (!is.null(p)) {
    ggsave(file.path(figures_dir, paste0("go_clusterprofiler_", pc_label, "10pct.png")),
           plot = p, width = 10, height = 9)
  }
}

cat("Done - results saved to output_tables/ and figures/\n")
```
